Let $Q$ be the amount of contaminants in the basin at time $t.$ Then, the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which contaminants enter the basin minus the rate at which contaminants leave the basin.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{lb}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which contaminants enter the basin.

Note that clean water (i.e., water containing $0\,\text{lb/gal}$ of contaminants) enters the basin at a rate of $24\,\text{gal/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *contaminants* enter the basin is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(0\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}})\cdot (24\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(0\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}})\cdot (24\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =0\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which contaminants exit the basin.

To find the rate at which contaminants leave the basin, we first determine the volume of wastewater in the basin at time $t.$

The basin initially contains $480\,\text{gal}$ of wastewater; water enters at $24\,\text{gal/min}$ and drains out at $18\,\text{gal/min}.$
As a result, the amount of wastewater in the basin after $t$ minutes is 

$$
480+24t-18t=(480+6t)\,\text{gal}.
$$

Since $Q$ is the amount of contaminants in the basin, the *concentration* of the wastewater at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{480+6t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed liquid leaves at a rate of $18\,\text{gal/min},$ *contaminants* leave at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(18\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{480+6t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}) \\  & =(18\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{480+6t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}}) \\  & =\frac{18Q}{480+6t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{3Q}{80+t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

The rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit. Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =0-\frac{3Q}{80+t}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}=-\frac{3}{80+t}\,Q.
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{Q}\cdot \frac{dQ}{dt} & =-\frac{3}{80+t} \\ \int \frac{1}{Q}\cdot \frac{dQ}{dt}dt & =\int (-\frac{3}{80+t})\,dt \\ \int \frac{1}{Q}\cdot \,dQ & =-3\int \frac{1}{80+t}\,dt \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|Q| & =-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|80+t|+C \\ |Q| & ={e}^{-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|80+t|+C} \\ Q(t) & =\frac{A}{(80+t)^{3}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $A=\pm {e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that the basin initially contains $12\,\text{lb}$ of contaminants. So, we can apply the initial condition $Q(0)=12,$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(0) & =12 \\ \frac{A}{(80+0)^{3}} & =12 \\ A & =12\cdot {80}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$

$$
Q(t)=12{(\frac{80}{80+t})}^{3}
$$

Finally, the amount of contaminants in the basin $10$ minutes after the clean water is first pumped in is

$$
Q(12)=12{(\frac{80}{90})}^{3}≈8.43\,\text{lb},
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

Qout′=(18galmin)⋅(Q480+6tlbgal)=(18galmin)⋅(Q480+6tlbgal)=18Q480+6tlbmin=3Q80+tlbmin.

Step 3: Calculate the overall rate of change.

dQdt=Qin′−Qout′=0−3Q80+t which gives the equation dQdt=−380+tQ.

Q(t)=12(8080+t)3
